title: A Wedding
strapline: Flowers, best clothes, music and a great big cake — a joyful celebration of two people coming together, however weddings look in your family.
intent: Weddings are joyful celebrations children often witness or hear about, and playing one out lets them explore a big, happy life event and the many different ways families celebrate love and commitment.
Meeting weddings from different cultures and family shapes — different clothes, foods, music and customs — grows respect for difference and reflects every kind of family.
Planning and hosting a wedding is cooperation in action — everyone with a job, from making invitations to laying the feast to the celebration dance.
The preparations weave in mathematics — counting guests, matching a place for each one, sharing the cake fairly, ordering the day.
Invitations, place cards, menus and a guest list give writing a real and happy purpose.
Rich language and knowledge grow — celebrate, guest, invite, bouquet, feast, music, together, promise.
implementation: Set up the makings of a celebration — dressing-up clothes, flowers, a feast table, music, a cake, cameras — and let children direct the event.
Take a guest role so children plan, invite, host, serve and celebrate, following their own ideas of how a wedding goes.
Draw on the real weddings children know — invite families to share their traditions, foods and clothes — so many kinds of celebration are welcome and respected.
Model the planning talk: 'How many guests are coming? So how many chairs and how many pieces of cake will we need?'
Leave invitations, place cards, a guest list and menu materials so writing and counting have a job to do.
Celebrate together with music, dancing and a shared feast, and let the story grow — the flowers, the photographs, the big day.
key_questions: How many guests are coming? So how many chairs will we need?
How many pieces of cake so everyone gets one?
What does a wedding look like in your family?
Who has a job today — who will make the invitations?
What order shall the day go in?

impact.text: Children explore a big, happy life event and the many different ways families celebrate love.
Children plan and host together — everyone with a job — in cooperation in action.
Children count guests, match a place for each and share the cake fairly.
Children make invitations, place cards, menus and a guest list, giving writing a real and happy purpose.
Children grow words and knowledge — celebrate, guest, invite, feast, together, promise.

enhancements: Dressing-up clothes, flowers, a feast table, music, a cake and cameras.
Families invited to share their traditions, foods and clothes.
Invitations, place cards, a guest list and menu materials for writing and counting.
Music, dancing and a shared feast to celebrate together.
A growing storyline — the flowers, the photographs, the big day.

playing_exploring: Children replay a big, joyful real event and bring their own families' celebrations and ideas into the play.
They dress up, decorate, host and celebrate wholeheartedly.
active_learning: Children plan and set up the whole celebration together, seeing the preparations through to the feast and the dance.
creating_thinking: Children work out how many guests, chairs and shares are needed, and invent their own version of the celebration.
